analyst.summary: Maruti's domestic demand cycle has turned favorably post-GST 2.0 (small-car GST cut from 29-31% to 18% effective 22-Sep-2025), with Q1 FY27 total sales up 29.3% YoY, June 2026 sales +19.3% YoY, record FY26 exports of 4.47 lakh units (+~34% YoY), and Kharkhoda's second line (commercial production from 18-May-2026) unlocking 26.5 lakh units/year total installed capacity -- a genuine, multi-engine volume story. Set against that: our own PIT quarterly data shows PBT margin compressing from ~13.5-14% (FY24/early-FY25) to 9.4% (Q4FY26), FY26 net profit grew only +1.2% YoY versus ~20% revenue growth, and PV market share fell to a 13-year low of 39.26% (three consecutive years of decline) on SUV under-representation, though June's UV growth (+28.7% YoY) is an early sign of stabilization. At ~29.5x trailing P/E the stock looks fairly valued rather than cheap or stretched -- consistent with the quant model's own Hold/Hold verdict -- pricing continued volume growth without requiring the margin story to fully repair. Call: Hold.
